reviews.title: Paid subscription without a warning!
reviews.text: I started using the app for 2 years when I started working out for the first time. On the 30th of December 2025, I went to the gym and I realized that the app was no longer free. All my workouts I have customized myself including the ones I took pictures of the equipment they do not have in the app to put in my routine have been blocked. I chose the app because it was free and I could create my own routines peacefully but now you have to pay. Honestly speaking that change messed up my entire experience with the app. I used to go the gym without worrying about logging in my reps, my sets, my rest time because everything was logged in. But now I can’t keep track of my progress anymore because of that. I do not even know my PR anymore, what I did the week before. It’s REALLY FRUSTRATING! Anything I touch in app, they asking me for a premium membership. Everything!! Nothing is free anymore nor basic to even use. I might as well delete the app because I have not used it since 9 months now. Please people do something because I want the app but not having access to anything without paying it, is annoying! Thank you!

reviews.title: Poorly motivational
reviews.text:
I have no idea who writes your “motivational messaging” but it sounds like you hired a frat bro.

Saying something like “someone weaker than you is now stronger than you because they worked out” is not motivational at all. You have zero idea why I and I imagine many others have not being able to go to the gym. 

I’ve kept the app because of the practical tracking and the videos on form but those two aspects are not difficult to replicate in a world of AI. It bugs me a lot the wording you’ve had for the last 2-3 months but this sent me over.

reviews.title: You won’t progress
reviews.text:
Interface is great. App is frustratingly dumb. As one single example, and there are many, It cannot differentiate between a set you did as your first workout of a day versus when it puts that same workout as sets 12-15. Because of this, your weight won’t increase unless you ignore the app. I’ve used it 3 years and I just have to ignore how stupid it is. To make matters worse, it tries to get saucy and add in a deload week every now and then. Great. But then it immediately forgets that your last data was from a deload, so that’s your new recommended weight going forward. Combine this with the fact that it wants to do 1 million different workouts, so you might not get back to that particular exercise for six months. When you come back you have to figure out the weight yourself because the app does not designate deload weeks in the data, and, again, you remember the app is so dumb as to not be trusted.

Second - it recommends workouts like somebody who’s never been to a gym. But for how AI the workouts feel, man is it dumb. Just so, so, frustratingly stupid.

reviews.title: Severely Limited Customization & Workout Logic
reviews.text: This app worked well for me at first, but once I started building my own workouts, the limitations became really frustrating. The customization options are extremely limited and sometimes confusing. For example, I couldn’t select something as basic as an assisted underhand pull-up, and creating functional movements is almost impossible. There’s no way to build exercises that use both time and weight, like a farmer’s carry. Even trying to create a simple sprint workout is restrictive — you’re forced into generic “running” options with set time increments instead of being able to program intervals properly. The exercise library also feels incomplete. There are missing machine exercises and not enough variety overall. It would be a huge improvement if users could submit custom exercises to be added to the app. On top of that, the auto-generated workouts don’t seem to follow solid training principles. A “back workout” will often include multiple variations of the same movement (like two different lat pulldowns) instead of providing balanced variety. There doesn’t seem to be much consideration for how to train different muscle groups effectively or structure a well-rounded workout. Overall, the app is a decent starting point, but it falls short if you’re trying to train with intention, variety, and proper programming.
